description: Everything that says what is in the way of the chat from outside it, as banners and bars around the Baude main window's chat column. One file, one part per banner. The chat banner is a single strip at the top of the chat column, above the find bar and the transcript, showing one message at a time (the first applicable in the order listed under parts); the others sit elsewhere as stated.

parts.name: chat banner
parts.shows: A full-width strip (an Adw banner) revealed with a slide under the header and above the chat, one title line (markup) and an optional button at its right. It is hidden when nothing applies. When several things apply, the one shown is the first of: host gone, chat missing, active elsewhere, connection dropped, API retrying, daemon/app older. The composer's send button is switched off while the host is gone, the chat is missing, or the connection dropped.

parts.name: host gone
parts.shows: A network chat whose host is out of reach: "Can't connect to <host> at the moment" ("Can't connect to <host> at the moment: <why>" when the last try said why) for a host that is down; "Looking for <host> on the network…" while it is being looked for; this machine's host is called Daemon ("Looking for daemon…"). No button. The viewed chat is shown as it was last seen. Where the operating system closes the app's link while it's put away (the phone; a web version's tab), a host lost a moment ago, or being reached again after the app is brought back, shows only a dim cloud and "Reconnecting…" centred over the chat, no strip, for its first 30 seconds; the strip with the reason comes after that, or at once for a reason a retry won't fix (the phone's key, its sign-in, no Baude commands on the host). The send button stays on: what's sent waits in the queue (see Composer).

decisions.said: 'Can't connect to <host>' confused when it was the user's own host; say 'daemon' instead.
decisions.rule: Every app calls its own machine's host the Daemon when it can't be reached ('Looking for daemon…'), and names another machine's host by name.

decisions.said: Nearly all of the phone's disconnects come from the screen turning off or the app being put away: design for Android closing connections, cache more, and instead of a red box show a cloud, with leeway and messages queued while the connection is down (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app whose link the OS or browser closes while it's put away gives a lost host 30 seconds of leeway (from when it went, or from when the app is brought back, whichever is later) shown as a quiet cloud and "Reconnecting…", never an alarming banner, and tries the link again the moment it's brought back or its network comes back; it says it can't connect only once the host has stayed away past the leeway, or at once for a reason a retry won't fix.

parts.name: host stopping
parts.shows: While the chat's host announces it is stopping or restarting (in place of gone or dropped): "<host> stopping…" or "<host> restarting…", with the count when known "<host> stopping — 2 of 3 processes to stop" (singular "process"), and "<host> stopping — every process stopped" at the end. This machine's host is named Daemon.

decisions.said: Quitting Baude's host process seems unresponsive; show how it's stopping, e.g. 'Daemon is restarting, X processes to kill' (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app shows a host's stop or restart from its first moment: "<host> stopping…" / "restarting…", then how many of its processes are still to stop, counting down

parts.name: chat missing on its host
parts.shows: The host is there but has no such session: "<Daemon or host> no longer has this chat", or "<name> couldn't take this chat up again: <reason>". Button "New chat" starts a new chat on that host.
text: {name} couldn't take this chat up again: {reason}

actions.does: Starts a new chat on that host

parts.name: active elsewhere
parts.shows: "This session is currently active elsewhere", no button. Shown for a Claude Desktop chat that Claude Desktop is writing to now: one on this machine, or a host's (its host says so: elsewhere), on every app; the composer is hidden meanwhile and what Desktop writes appears live in the transcript with a spinner while it works. Goes when its transcript has been quiet. Other chats (host's, other windows', terminals') never show this.
text: This session is currently active elsewhere

decisions.said: Claude Desktop's chats are shared over the mesh so other hosts can see them and carry them on
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a host's Claude Desktop chat read-only, with this banner and no text box, while its host says Claude Desktop is writing it (elsewhere); otherwise writing in it takes it up on its host.

parts.name: connection dropped
parts.shows: "Connection to <daemon or host> dropped..." with the three dots stepping (every 0.35 s); the send button is off. Cleared when attached again (retried about every 10 s); the host leaving the network shows "host gone" instead. A turn that was running goes on on the host, and a message sent after a claude that exited notes "— resumed from <reason> —".

parts.name: API retrying
parts.shows: While claude retries the model's API: "The API returned <status>: retrying, attempt 2 of 5" or "The API didn't answer: retrying" (attempt part only when known), dots stepping; gone when the next thing arrives or the turn ends.
text: The API returned {status}: retrying, attempt {n} of {max}

parts.name: daemon or app older
parts.shows: This Mac's host process (daemon) and Baude running different code, when nothing about the chat itself is in the way: "Baude is older than its daemon" (button "Restart Baude"), "Daemon is older than Baude" (button "Restart Daemon"), "Baude and its daemon are out of date" (button "Restart Both"), or for another checkout's code "Daemon runs the code in <folder>" / "Daemon runs another checkout's code" (button "Dismiss"). Said after the difference has lasted a while (at once for another checkout). Not said while an Update button already says it.

phone.why: Restarting this Mac's host process and the desktop app that talks to it

actions.does: Restarts Baude, the daemon (once no command is running on it; an idle model turn is cut short and offered Continue) or both; the Dismiss button just stops the message. A toast "Restarting the daemon once N sessions finish running a command" while it waits, "Daemon restarted" after

decisions.said: 'Local's host process is older than Baude' was useless copy: say 'Daemon is older than client', 'Restart Daemon?', then 'Daemon restarted'.
decisions.rule: Every app calls its own machine's host process the Daemon when the two run different code ('Daemon is older than <app>', button 'Restart Daemon', toast 'Daemon restarted'), never by the host's name.

parts.name: update bar
parts.shows: At the foot of the sessions sidebar, under a rule: a flat left-aligned button "Update", shown while a new version waits to be restarted onto. Hidden when no update waits.

phone.does: The phone's own updater: the Update bar at the foot of home (Update.kt)
phone.why: The phone installs builds, not a git checkout

actions.does: Tooltip "A new version is ready" when nothing is in the way; else "Waiting for:" then a bulleted line per blocker ("• running: <command>", "• a side question's reply being written", "• a dialog open", "• you, using this window", "• local's host process: <command>")
Restarts onto the new version. If that would stop running commands, first asks "Restart now?" listing them with Cancel and "Restart Now" (destructive style); stopped chats can be continued after

text: The new version is picked up now. These are stopped, and their chats can be continued after:

parts.name: host state note
parts.shows: Over the sidebar's chat list (not the chat column): a small outlined island, text centred and wrapped, slid down, saying why the host picked beside New session can't be reached: "Looking for <host> on the network…", "Can't connect to <host> at the moment[: why]", "<host> is deactivated", or its stopping/restarting line. The host's chats stay listed as they were last seen. Gone when the host is there. Where the operating system closes the app's link (the phone), a host away less than 30 seconds shows a dim cloud and "Reconnecting…" instead, its chats listed as they were, not dimmed.

decisions.said: The host's can't-connect message was a banner flush at the left and not at the right; it should be a rounded island like the empty states
decisions.rule: Every app draws a host's can't-reach note over the chat list as a small outlined rounded island, text centred, never a banner flush with one edge.

decisions.said: Nearly all of the phone's disconnects come from the screen turning off or the app being put away: design for Android closing connections, cache more, and instead of a red box show a cloud, with leeway and messages queued while the connection is down (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app whose link the OS closes lists a host's chats as last seen, not dimmed or crossed out, with a cloud and "Reconnecting…" over them, while the host has been away less than the leeway; the can't-connect island and crossed-out clouds come after it.

parts.name: cut short by a restart line
parts.shows: At the end of the transcript (a chat line, not a banner): dim "Cut short by a restart" with a button "Continue" (tooltip sends the continue message); after pressing, a spinner and "Continuing…". Shown for a turn a restart cut short, until something is sent.

actions.does: Sends the continue message to the chat

parts.name: toasts
parts.shows: Short messages at the bottom of the window that go by themselves after a few seconds: "Transcript copied", "That session was deleted on <host>", Signal on/off notes (with a Show button), the zoom toast (see Shortcuts), held-send refusals (see Composer).

states.name: no banner
states.shows: The strip is hidden, no room is taken
